Data contamination and leakage risks are insufficiently addressed. DIM-T2I is web-crawled without deduplication against benchmarks, and DIM-Edit CoTs are generated with access to target images, which complicates claims about real inference-time planning.

The human quality study is too small for a 233K-sample dataset: only 100 examples are inspected, with no inter-annotator agreement or uncertainty estimates. The larger quality assessment is again performed by an MLLM.
The paper lacks an adequate ethics and data governance discussion for 14M web images and image-editing technology, including copyright, privacy, harmful edits, consent, and bias/misuse concerns.

Several claims are overstated. The method is weak on text editing, logic/geometric editing, and reference-free transformations, and on GEdit-Bench overall it trails Step1X-Edit; the paper’s SOTA framing does not sufficiently reflect these limitations.
